subject: mathematics
question_text: Find the vector equation of the line passing through the point 2i + j + 3k and parallel to the vector 4i − 2j + 3k.

recall_prompt: Say the vector equation of a line through a point and parallel to a vector.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Name the point and direction
steps.margin_note: First mark. Two different things are given: a point the line passes THROUGH, and a direction it runs ALONG. Name them apart before writing anything.

recall.must_convey: That the given point is named a and the parallel vector b — a position and a direction, kept separate.
accept: call the point a and the parallel vector b
name the position vector a and the direction vector b
one is the point on the line and the other is the direction
point ni a, parallel vector ni b ani peru pettali
identify which is the point and which is the direction

steps.why: The formula treats the two completely differently — one is added once, the other is scaled by the parameter. Mixing them up gives a different line.
common_mistakes: Treating the parallel vector as a second point on the line.
Adding the two vectors together first.

steps.label: Write the equation
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The form is r = a + tb: start at the point, then travel any distance along the direction. t ranges over all real numbers.
lines: Vector equation of the line is

recall.must_convey: That the equation is r = a + tb with t real, written out with the given vectors.
accept: r equals a plus t b where t is any real number
the equation is the point plus t times the direction
r equals two i plus j plus three k plus t times four i minus two j plus three k
r equals a plus t b, t real number
write the point plus parameter times the parallel vector
heard_as: r equals a plus t b

steps.why: Every point of the line is reached by choosing some t: t = 0 gives the given point, and the rest sweep out the line in both directions.
common_mistakes: Writing r = ta + b, which swaps the roles.
Omitting "t ∈ R", which leaves the equation describing one point.
